title: Redeeming Wanderlane Traveller Club Points Against a Travel Booking
content:
Wanderlane Traveller Club points are redeemed against a travel booking at the redemption value of the tier held, and a redemption below the tier's minimum is refused rather than rounded up. Points are spent only while the membership record stands at active. The membership record is the authority for that standing, read against this membership before the points are spent.

A redemption is settled in points only; the balance of the price is collected in money and a booking is never held part-paid. Points on a suspended card may not be spent, and points on a closed card are forfeited without payment of any kind.

A member who has made more than the annual ceiling of 24 redemptions is referred to the programme office before any further redemption, because the pattern requires review. The redemptions counted are those on this same membership over the rolling 12 months ending on the day the request is handled, counted back day by day from that day.

## What the points are worth

The money the points carry against the booking is the number of points redeemed multiplied by the value of one point at the tier held, expressed in US cents and converted to US dollars at one hundred cents to the dollar. In a hypothetical case, a member redeems 12000 points at a tier whose point is worth 1.15 US cents: the points carry 13800 US cents, which is 138.00 US dollars against the price of the booking, and the rest of the price is collected in money.

## The card's standing, and what may be done

| Standing of the membership record | Whether points may be spent |
| --- | --- |
| active | Points may be spent |
| suspended | Points may not be spent |
| closed | Points are forfeited without payment of any kind |
| Any other standing of the record | Points are not spent, because points are spent only while the record stands at active |

## Points of judgement

*A member asks to redeem a number of points that falls just below the minimum of the tier held.* The redemption is refused. It is not rounded up to the minimum, and the shortfall is not made good in money.

*A member asks to redeem exactly the minimum of the tier held.* That redemption is not below the minimum, and it is not refused on that ground.

*A member offers to pay part of the balance in points and leave the rest of the booking unpaid until later.* A booking is never held part-paid: the points settle what they settle, and the balance of the price is collected in money.
